extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians/authors preparing submissions to the journal Mathematics of Computation (American Mathematical Society)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and requirements for preparing and submitting research articles to the AMS journal Mathematics of Computation, including scope, submission procedures, and post-acceptance obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aims and scope / topical suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles must be of significant computational interest and contain original and substantial mathematical analysis or development of computational methodology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Areas covered include numerical analysis, computational discrete mathematics (including number theory, algebra and combinatorics), and related fields such as stochastic numerical methods. Submissions not suitable by subject matter may be rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality / prior publication
rubrics_metrics.description: No paper that has been previously published, or is being considered for publication elsewhere, should be submitted to the American Mathematical Society, nor may a paper that is under consideration by the American Mathematical Society be submitted elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must ensure exclusivity of submission during the review period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission frequency limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are limited to three submissions within any 12-month period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This limit applies to submissions to Mathematics of Computation and is stated twice in the submission information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review model
rubrics_metrics.description: All articles appearing in this journal are peer reviewed by external reviewers. Mathematics of Computation has a single-anonymous peer-review process in which the reviewers know who the authors of the manuscript are, but the authors do not have access to the information on who the peer reviewers are.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions about the initial submission process should be directed to the journal contact email. Note editors may handle suitability before external review (see 'Editors may reject without external review').

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial pre-screening (desk rejection) criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors may reject papers without external review that are not suitable for publication in the journal due to reasons such as subject matter or clear weaknesses in scientific content or presentation style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear weaknesses in scientific content OR in presentation style (i.e., poor exposition) are grounds for immediate rejection without sending the manuscript to external referees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: An abstract is required. It must be brief, reasonably self-contained, and not exceed 300 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The AMS offers free worldwide access to the electronic abstracts. Prepare an abstract that stands alone and summarizes the work concisely (<=300 words).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematics Subject Classification (MSC) requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Included with the footnotes to the paper should be the 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification representing the primary and secondary subjects of the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide correct MSC codes (primary and secondary) from the 2020 scheme as part of the manuscript metadata/footnotes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred submission method / file format
rubrics_metrics.description: The preferred method of submission is to upload a PDF file using the Initial Manuscript Submission form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The AMS uses Centralized Manuscript Processing for initial submissions. Use the online form and upload a PDF to avoid delays; alternate postal submission is possible but not preferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required information for mailed (paper) submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: If a paper copy is being forwarded to the AMS, the following information is required: Name of the journal to which the paper is submitted; Name of the corresponding author; Contact information including email address and mailing address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All contact information, particularly email addresses, must be supplied to avoid delay. The author should also suggest an appropriate Editor to review the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggesting an appropriate editor
rubrics_metrics.description: The author should suggest an appropriate Editor to review the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When submitting (especially by mail), indicate which Editor you think is suitable; this assists centralized processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-acceptance: Consent to Publish and copyright
rubrics_metrics.description: All authors must submit the Consent to Publish. All authors must agree regarding the Copyright Agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the article is to be published in one of the AMS Open Access journals, authors must agree which Creative Commons License will be selected. Follow the online Submission Instructions after acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use AMS style files and resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are encouraged to use AMS-prepared style files in preparing their papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The AMS Author Resource Center provides TeX Resources, the AMS Style Guide, the Mathematics Subject Classification, journal abbreviations for bibliographies, and AMS journal article templates from Overleaf. Using these resources improves conformity to AMS formatting expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and editorial assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Language editing services available from Charlesworth Author Services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors for whom English is not a first language or who want professional copyediting may consider these services to improve presentation quality and reduce risk of desk rejection for poor presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparing graphics and accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance/tools available for preparing graphics and accessible mathematics content (Joint Author Guidelines for Preparing Accessible Mathematics Content; Preparing graphics).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow AMS guidance to prepare figures and ensure mathematical content is accessible (e.g., for screen readers) as part of good presentation practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offprints / author electronic access after publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Offprints are provided free of charge in electronic form to all authors. A downloadable and printable PDF version of each article is available from the AMS website following print publication. Notification email containing access information is sent to all authors as soon as an issue is published in print.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This describes the post-publication access authors receive and the electronic delivery system providing authors with permanent electronic access to their published material.
